Looking at the test image, I can see a split corn stalk with:
- Shredded internal pith
- Visible stringy vascular tissue
- Tan to brown discoloration of the interior tissue

This is clearly a stalk rot disease. Let me examine reference images for the main stalk rot candidates.

Analyzing the test image and reference materials:

**Test Image Features:**
- Split stalk revealing shredded internal pith
- Tan to brown discoloration of interior tissue
- Visible stringy vascular strands intact
- Macerated (broken down) pith tissue
- No obvious external blackening or charring
- No mushy/wet appearance

**Comparison to candidates:**
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Shows gray/charred appearance with very thin threads—test image is more brown-tan
- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Displays heavy external stalk blackening and shiny black streaks—not prominent in test image
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: Characteristic tan-brown discolored macerated pith with visible vascular strands—**MATCHES test image**
- **Bacterial stalk rot**: Appears mushy/slimy with softer tissue—test image appears more fibrous
- **Physoderma stalk rot**: Primarily node blackening with snapping—test image shows general pith deterioration

The tan to brown discoloration of the macerated internal pith, with visible stringy vascular tissue remaining, is diagnostic for **Diplodia stalk rot**.
